moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
learningObjectives: Explain the role of the Business Architect with respect to the Business and IT project teams.
Describe how the Business Architect liaises with project stakeholders.
Articulate how essential competencies of a Business Architect contribute to achieving successful outcomes in Pega implementation projects.

elements.description: The liaison who bridges the client organization and the Pega delivery team, understanding business needs and Pega capabilities to produce software that exceeds what either side could build alone.
On a Pega project, the BA belongs to both the Business team (process and organizational needs) and the IT team (software development and Pega capabilities), bridging the two groups.
'Client' or 'organization' is the business transforming its workflows with Pega. 'Customer' is that business's end customer. Exam scenarios deliberately swap these terms to test precision.

elements.text: The Bilingual Diplomat: A BA stands between two delegations that speak different languages — Business (customer outcomes and process pain) and IT (Rules, Cases, and Pega capabilities). The BA translates both ways so the treaty they sign — the application — truly serves everyone.

bulletPoints: A well-designed, well-implemented application must meet business requirements, achieve the strategic objective, AND delight the end customer.
A key BA goal is to identify WHAT must change in the current process and HOW current issues affect business outcomes.
The BA both advocates for the business's needs and advocates for Pega's software-development capabilities and the redesigned process.

elements.description: Gather a complete picture of problems before configuring a solution: understand critical stages, identify bottlenecks and workarounds, diagnose root causes, and find functionality common across processes.
Optimize the workflow using Pega GenAI Blueprint: remove unnecessary steps, re-sequence stages, automate repetitive activities, intelligently allocate work, and consolidate data for users.
Collaborate with Business and IT to design, build, and test the solution using Blueprint and App Studio, ensuring both sides understand requirements and the proposed workflow improvements.
Continuously teach Business stakeholders the value of Pega's out-of-the-box features, helping them focus on outcomes rather than current methods and become advocates for the new process.

elements.text: A relay race where one runner never stops: Analysis hands to Process Design, which hands to Alignment, which hands to Education — but Education keeps lapping the track the whole project, continually enabling stakeholders to change how they work.

bulletPoints: Process Design is explicitly Blueprint-driven in the current curriculum — the BA translates insight INTO Blueprint, not hand-drawn flows.
Analysis goal: know what needs to change and how issues affect outcomes. Process Design goal: ensure the new Blueprint workflow meets objectives and simplifies the process for end users.
Alignment goal: the Business team understands the design and gives the right guidance, while Pega developers deeply understand business needs and can advise on the best use of Pega capabilities.
Education goal: enable stakeholders to change their ways of working using Pega features, achieve business value, and realize the benefits of their application.

elements.text: Sara Han, a Pega BA on a complaints-management project, is asked to review the process so the business resolves concerns faster. She EDUCATES stakeholders on OOTB features (e.g., automatically routing work to the right users with business rules; distributing approval notifications by email and mobile) and explains how these reduce resolution time, improving customer satisfaction and business value. She ALIGNS with Business representatives to redesign the workflow and with IT to configure OOTB features, introducing automated, skill-based work allocation and SLA logic/notifications for faster resolution.

bulletPoints: The example shows two of the four responsibilities in action: Education (explaining OOTB value) and Alignment (redesign + configure with both teams).
Concrete OOTB features cited: rule-based automatic routing, email/mobile notifications, skill-based allocation, and Service-Level Agreement logic.

elements.description: Organize and facilitate focused meetings with stakeholders and SMEs to gather and document business processes and requirements, guiding stakeholder understanding by translating how OOTB Pega features meet business requirements.

Document business requirements as user stories using Blueprint, App Studio's Agile workbench, and other Scrum tools. Pega developers (System Architects) use those user stories to configure the application to make the best use of Pega's strengths.

Use Blueprint to quickly redesign a workflow based on OOTB features and case-management best practices (building stakeholder alignment), and use App Studio to demonstrate how additional Pega features address requirements.

Across the project landscape — organizational structure, user-story and backlog creation, governance, and testing — the BA follows and instructs on Pega's proven best practices throughout design and delivery.

bulletPoints: Team size varies: large projects use multiple BAs sharing the load; a small project may need only one BA.
Senior BAs may also own: risk management, governance, UI development, reporting, standard setting, stakeholder analysis, project scoping/sizing, testing, or production support.
All BAs should harness opportunities to learn these additional, often senior-level, tasks.
Tool reference for documenting requirements: the Pega Express Toolkit.

elements.description: A client Business-team representative primarily responsible for managing project SCOPE and PRIORITIZING requirements throughout development. The BA runs user-story review meetings with the PO to finalize acceptance criteria and prioritize the backlog so desired features land in the timeline.
The project manager who leads the Pega delivery team, maintains governance, and liaises with client leadership on timeline, budget, and scope — the BA works with the PDL on governance decisions.
Promotes and supports Scrum; organizes the team, facilitates ceremonies (Sprint Planning, Sizing, Backlog Refinement, Retrospective), and is accountable for team success and removing blockers.
The Pega developers (SA, SSA, LSA) who configure the application. The LSA imports the Blueprint and configures requirements from user stories; BAs translate technical information for stakeholders.

Ensure functionality meets documented requirements. QAs build test scripts from user stories, participate in sizing, and flag defects. The BA helps decide if a flagged item is a defect or a new requirement.

bulletPoints: PO = scope & backlog priority; PDL = delivery lead, governance, timeline/budget; Scrum Master = ceremonies & unblocking.
System Architects (SA/SSA/LSA) configure the application; the LSA imports the Blueprint.
QAs test against user stories; the BA helps triage defects vs. new requirements.

elements.description: Client representatives with first-hand knowledge of the business process steps. BAs collaborate with SMEs in an operational walkthrough to observe the as-is process and capture all work, in and out of the system.

Client representatives primarily responsible for documenting the current 'as-is' process, data requirements, and business requirements. The BA reviews this documentation to identify redundancies and bottlenecks, recommend automations, determine resource needs, and define data/interface details.

Ensure the design meets end-user needs, complies with accessibility standards, and delivers a consistent experience across all delivery Channels. The BA collaborates to align the UI with UX requirements, maximize OOTB features, and meet business objectives.

Works with the client during the initial sales phase, often designing the Blueprint with stakeholders, then transitions the Blueprint to the delivery BAs and System Architects before the project starts.

bulletPoints: SME = first-hand step knowledge via operational walkthrough; Business Analyst = documents the as-is process and data.
UX Designers ensure accessible, consistent experiences across channels.
Solutions Consultant = pre-sales; designs the Blueprint and transitions it to the delivery team.

elements.description: A secure, private space for one operator to build and manage features in one application independently. Changes stay private until shared to a Branch, preventing rule conflicts during parallel development.

A Ruleset container for rapidly changing records, letting teams develop features in isolation. One Branch per feature is the standard strategy; changes are only shared once stable, conflict-free, and approved.
When importing a Blueprint into Pega Platform, all assets are created in a Branch except Access Roles, which are handled separately outside the Branch.

elements.text: Workspace vs. Branch: a Workspace is your private sketchpad — only you see it; a Branch is the shared drafting table where a feature's pages are assembled with the team before being bound into the final book (the merged Ruleset).

bulletPoints: Workspace = one operator + one application; private until shared to a Branch; enabled via EnableWorkspace.
Some Rule types may still require Dev Studio access depending on permissions.
Branch = Ruleset container for rapid change; standard strategy is one Branch per feature; beneficial when feature completion times differ.
Blueprint import creates assets in a Branch — EXCEPT Access Roles.

elements.description: Break down complex business processes and identify opportunities for improvement and simplification.
Process design skills and knowledge of business process design to innovate new processes and ways of working that achieve the outcome.

elements.term: Systems design, Pega technology & Blueprint knowledge
elements.description: Understand Pega's architecture, out-of-the-box features, and Blueprint so business requirements and end-user needs can be mapped to the right Pega capabilities and solutions.
Create a common language and shared understanding of both the business need and Pega's capabilities across the project team and stakeholders.
Help the Business team embrace the new Pega solution and become advocates for it within their organization.

bulletPoints: The BA is the crucial link keeping stakeholders engaged, aligned, and communicating effectively.
These five skill areas combine with experience to guide Business and IT to innovate and achieve outcomes.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing 'Client' with 'Customer'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Scenario questions swap these terms. 'Client/organization' is the business implementing Pega to transform a workflow; 'customer' is that business's END customer.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If the entity is paying Pega to transform a workflow, it is the client; if it is being served by that workflow, it is the customer.

examPitfalls.title: Who imports the Blueprint?
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates attribute Blueprint import to the BA or a generic SA. The curriculum specifies the LEAD System Architect (LSA) imports the Blueprint file into the environment.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: BAs and Blueprint create user stories; the LSA imports the Blueprint and configures functional/technical requirements from those stories.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint import and Access Roles
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A subtle fact: importing a Blueprint creates all assets in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If asked which asset is NOT created in the Branch on Blueprint import, the answer is Access Roles.

examPitfalls.title: Workspace scope assumptions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions imply a Workspace can span multiple apps or operators, or that changes are visible to others immediately.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Workspace = exactly one operator + one application, private until shared to a Branch. A Branch is the shared feature container.

examPitfalls.title: Process Design = Blueprint, not manual flows or coding
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Distractors describe the BA hand-building flows or writing code. The current curriculum frames Process Design around Pega GenAI Blueprint applying best practices.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Associate Process Design with Blueprint-driven redesign: remove waste, re-sequence, automate, intelligently allocate, consolidate data.

examPitfalls.title: PO vs. PDL vs. Scrum Master responsibilities
examPitfalls.trapDescription: These three are easily conflated. PO = scope & backlog priority; PDL = delivery lead, governance, timeline/budget; Scrum Master = facilitates Scrum ceremonies and removes blockers.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Map the verb: prioritize scope → PO; protect timeline/budget & governance → PDL; run ceremonies/unblock → Scrum Master.

examPitfalls.title: SME vs. Business Analyst
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Both are client representatives. The SME has first-hand step knowledge (operational walkthrough); the Business Analyst documents the 'as-is' process, data, and requirements.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Need to OBSERVE how the work is actually done → SME. Need the documented 'as-is' process/data → Business Analyst.

examPitfalls.title: Where the Solutions Consultant fits
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The Solutions Consultant is a pre-sales role, not a delivery role; questions test that they design the Blueprint early and then hand it off.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Solutions Consultant = sales phase; designs the Blueprint with the client, then transitions it to BAs and SAs before delivery starts.

examPitfalls.title: The four responsibilities are not interchangeable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Scenarios describe an activity and ask which responsibility it belongs to. Teaching OOTB value = Education; redesigning with both teams = Alignment; gathering/diagnosing the current process = Analysis; optimizing the workflow in Blueprint = Process Design.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Match the verb to A-P-A-E: diagnose=Analysis, optimize-in-Blueprint=Process Design, collaborate-to-build=Alignment, teach=Education.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A regional bank hires Pega to transform its loan-origination workflow. A teammate says 'the customer needs the new field validated.' In Pega BA terminology, who is the 'client' in this engagement?

options.text: The bank implementing Pega to transform its workflow
The individual loan applicant served by the workflow
The Pega System Architect configuring the application

practiceQuiz.hint: The client transforms its workflow; the customer is the end user it serves.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The bank is the client/organization. The loan applicant is the 'customer.' The SA is a delivery-team member and Pegasystems is the vendor — neither is the 'client.'

practiceQuiz.scenario: After Blueprint-based design is approved, a file must be brought into the Pega Platform environment to scaffold the application's assets. Who is responsible for importing the Blueprint?
practiceQuiz.hint: The most senior member of the System Architect family.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The LSA imports the Blueprint and configures functional/technical requirements using the user stories. The PO manages scope, the BA authors stories and aligns teams, and the Scrum Master facilitates ceremonies.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA must gather the exact mandatory steps of an 'as-is' fraud-detection process and later confirm the redesigned 'to-be' process meets operational needs. Which TWO stakeholders are most appropriate for this objective?
practiceQuiz.hint: One has first-hand step knowledge; the other documents the current 'as-is' process and data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: SMEs provide first-hand operational/functional step knowledge (operational walkthrough) and Business Analysts document the 'as-is' process, data, and requirements. QAs build tests from stories; the Solutions Consultant is pre-sales. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer needs a private space where their changes stay isolated until they are ready to share with the team. Which capability matches this, and what is its scope?

options.text: A Branch, tied to one operator and one application
A Workspace, tied to one operator and one application, private until shared to a Branch
A Ruleset, which automatically merges changes across all teams
An Access Group, which isolates rules per operator

practiceQuiz.hint: The 'private until shared' detail is the giveaway.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Workspace is tied to exactly one operator and one application and stays private until shared to a Branch. A Branch is the shared feature container; Rulesets store/identify rules; Access Groups govern access.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During a Blueprint import into Pega Platform, the system creates the application's assets in a Branch. Which asset type is the exception that is NOT created in the Branch?
practiceQuiz.hint: It relates to security/permissions rather than workflow or UI.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Importing a Blueprint creates all assets in a Branch except Access Roles. Case Types, data objects, and Views are all created within the Branch; only Access Roles fall outside it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A stakeholder asks what the BA actually does during the 'Process Design' responsibility on a modern Pega project. Which TWO statements best describe it?

options.text: Translate analysis into a redesigned workflow using Pega GenAI Blueprint, applying Pega best practices
Automate repetitive activities and intelligently allocate work to the right users
Personally write the Java classes that implement the workflow logic
Import the production database schema and map physical tables

practiceQuiz.hint: Process Design is Blueprint-driven and outcome-focused — not hand-coding.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Process Design uses Blueprint to remove waste, re-sequence work, automate repetitive activities, and intelligently allocate work. Writing Java and mapping DB tables are System Architect implementation tasks. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA spends a session diagnosing bottlenecks, manual workarounds, and root causes in a client's current claims process before any design begins. Which of the four core responsibilities is this?
practiceQuiz.hint: It happens before configuring any solution — diagnosing the current state.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Diagnosing gaps, bottlenecks, workarounds, and root causes in the existing process is Analysis. Process Design optimizes via Blueprint, Alignment collaborates to build/test, and Education teaches OOTB value.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA explains to the Business team how Pega's automatic, rule-based routing and email/mobile approval notifications will cut complaint-resolution time and raise customer satisfaction. Which responsibility is the BA performing?
practiceQuiz.hint: Teaching stakeholders the value of Pega's out-of-the-box features.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Explaining the value of OOTB features to the Business team is Education. Analysis is diagnosing the current process; risk management/sizing are not among the four core responsibilities (sizing is a Scrum activity).

practiceQuiz.scenario: Scope for a fraud-detection app has grown and may affect the delivery timeline and budget. With whom does the BA primarily work to assess timeline impact and govern the change?

options.text: The Project Delivery Lead (PDL), along with the PO

practiceQuiz.hint: Who leads delivery, governance, timeline, and budget on the project?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The PDL leads the delivery team and governance and works with the PO (and sponsors) on scope/timeline/budget changes. UX, QA, and the (pre-sales) Solutions Consultant are not the governance owners here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA needs the documented current 'as-is' process and the details of how, when, and from where customer credit-history data is retrieved. Which stakeholder is the best source?
practiceQuiz.hint: Who documents the 'as-is' process and data requirements?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Business Analyst documents the current 'as-is' process, data, and business requirements, including data access details. The Scrum Master facilitates process, the PO owns scope/priority, and the UX Designer owns experience design.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA wants to OBSERVE how end users actually navigate the current application and capture work done both inside and outside the system. What activity, and with whom?

options.text: An operational walkthrough with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
A Sprint Retrospective with the Scrum Master
A backlog refinement with the Product Owner
A test-script review with the QA

practiceQuiz.hint: Observing the real 'as-is' steps points to a specific stakeholder.
practiceQuiz.rationale: BAs collaborate with SMEs in an operational walkthrough to observe the 'as-is' process and capture all work, in and out of system. The other ceremonies/reviews serve different purposes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Early in the SALES process, someone designs a Blueprint prototype with business stakeholders and later hands it to the delivery BAs and SAs. Which role is this?
practiceQuiz.hint: This person operates during the sales phase, before delivery begins.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Solutions Consultant works during the sales phase, often designs the Blueprint with stakeholders, then transitions it to BAs and SAs before delivery. The LSA imports/configures it later during delivery.

practiceQuiz.scenario: List the four CORE responsibilities of a Pega BA. Which THREE of the following belong to that core set?
practiceQuiz.hint: The four core are A-P-A-E; one option is only a possible senior add-on duty.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The four core responsibilities are Analysis, Process Design, Alignment, and Education. Production support is among the ADDITIONAL duties senior BAs may take on — not part of the core four. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A QA notifies the BA of a potential defect. The BA reviews it and concludes it is actually new desired behavior, not a flaw in the current design. What should happen next?

options.text: Present it to the Product Owner to consider for current or future scope
Immediately import a new Blueprint to fix it
Escalate it to the Solutions Consultant

practiceQuiz.hint: New requirement decisions are about scope and priority.
practiceQuiz.rationale: If the item is a new requirement rather than a defect, it is a scope/priority decision for the Product Owner. Blueprint import, the pre-sales Solutions Consultant, and deleting tests do not address a scope decision.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A small project cannot staff every role separately. Which statement reflects Pega's guidance on team structure?

options.text: One person may fill multiple roles — for example, the BA may also act as Product Owner
Every project must have a dedicated person for each role or it cannot start
Only Lead System Architects may hold more than one role
The customer must fill any unstaffed role

practiceQuiz.hint: Team size varies, so roles can overlap on smaller engagements.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Team structure varies; on smaller projects a single person may perform multiple roles (e.g., BA also acting as PO). The other statements are not supported by the curriculum.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new BA wants to know which capabilities support PARALLEL development so multiple developers don't overwrite each other. Which TWO are correct?

options.text: Workspaces give each operator a private space whose changes are hidden until shared to a Branch
A Branch isolates a feature's Ruleset changes until they are stable, conflict-free, and approved
Access Groups merge every developer's changes automatically in real time
A single shared Workspace is used by the entire team at once

practiceQuiz.hint: One mechanism is private per operator; the other isolates a feature for the team.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Workspaces keep an operator's changes private until shared to a Branch, and Branches isolate feature-level Ruleset changes until stable/approved. Access Groups govern access (they don't auto-merge), and a Workspace is tied to ONE operator, not shared by the team. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new Business Architect is presenting their responsibilities to a project sponsor who asks how long the education duty lasts. Which statement about Education as a BA responsibility is MOST accurate?

options.text: It is continuous throughout the project, enabling stakeholders to change their ways of working with Pega features
It happens only once, during project kickoff
It means writing the application's technical documentation for developers
It is the responsibility of the Scrum Master, not the BA

practiceQuiz.hint: Think of the relay runner that never stops.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Education is ongoing throughout the project — continually enabling business stakeholders to adopt Pega ways of working and realize value. It is not one-time, not developer documentation, and is a BA responsibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA documents a confirmed business need so System Architects can estimate effort and build it. In what form does the BA capture this requirement?

options.text: As a user story, using Blueprint and App Studio's Agile workbench
As a raw SQL script for the database team

practiceQuiz.hint: Requirements are captured in a specific Agile artifact using Pega tooling.
practiceQuiz.rationale: BAs document business requirements as user stories using Blueprint, App Studio's Agile workbench, and Scrum tooling; SAs then use those stories to size and configure. SQL, Access Roles, and Java artifacts are not how requirements are captured.

quickRecap.value: The bridge/liaison between the client's Business team and the Pega IT team; a member of both.
Analysis, Process Design (via Blueprint), Alignment, Education.
Client = the business implementing Pega. Customer = that business's end customer.
Performed by the Lead System Architect (LSA); creates all assets in a Branch EXCEPT Access Roles.
One operator + one application; changes private until shared to a Branch; enabled via EnableWorkspace.
Ruleset container for rapid change; standard strategy is one Branch per feature.
PO = scope & backlog priority; PDL = delivery lead, governance, timeline/budget; Scrum Master = ceremonies & unblocking.
SME = first-hand step knowledge via operational walkthrough; Business Analyst = documents the 'as-is' process and data.
Pre-sales; often designs the Blueprint, then transitions it to BAs and SAs for delivery.
System Architects (SA/SSA/LSA), Quality Analysts, UX Designers.
Analytical/problem-solving; process design; systems design/Pega/Blueprint; active listening/communication/facilitation; business-change knowledge.
